subject: Mali-G610 CSF MCU start: writes panthor performs vs writes present in hakios.mali610.c

registers.name: MCU_CONTROL
registers.panthor_write: MCU_CONTROL_AUTO (2) at panthor_fw.c:1143; MCU_CONTROL_DISABLE (0) at panthor_fw.c:1175
registers.note: Value and address agree. Nothing in the write itself differs.

registers.name: GPUEB CMD_POWER_CONTROL IPI
registers.panthor_write: mt6895_gpueb_power_on() called immediately before MCU_CONTROL=AUTO
registers.panthor_evidence: panthor_fw.c:1129-1143 (call site), panthor_device.c:256-268 (earlier call, before any GPU register touch)
registers.note: Driver never sends an IPI. Log line 'gpueb: not mapped' is a consequence of mali_gpueb=0 default (hakios.mali610.c:4290-4292), not evidence about GPUEB state.

registers.name: MCU_STATUS
registers.panthor_write: read only; read at panthor_fw.c:1156 for the failure message
registers.note: Agrees. Our reading 1 == MCU_STATUS_ENABLED, which panthor treats as boot failure, not success.

registers.name: JOB_INT_MASK
registers.panthor_write: pirq->mask, i.e. an enable mask; ~0 (all bits) written by panthor_job_irq_enable_events before AUTO
registers.panthor_evidence: panthor_fw.c:1128, panthor_device.h:582-583 (resume writes INT_CLEAR then INT_MASK=mask), panthor_device.h:605-618
registers.ours_write: 0x1008 <- 0xffffffff at :3148; 0x1008 <- 0 at :3992 (only after a successful boot)
registers.note: Semantics: bit set in INT_MASK means the event is DELIVERED (mask register holds the enable set), not blocked. Our :3148 write of 0xffffffff therefore ENABLES everything and matches panthor; the comment at :3989-3990 that calls it 'masking' is wrong. Consequence: JOB_INT_STATUS was readable throughout, so the all-zero 0x100c reading is a real hardware result, not a self-inflicted mask.

registers.name: GPU_IRQ_MASK
registers.panthor_write: GPU_INTERRUPTS_MASK via panthor_gpu_irq_enable_events (panthor_gpu.c:177)
registers.note: Same polarity conclusion as JOB_INT_MASK. 0x00080503 includes bit 10 (POWER_CHANGED_ALL).

registers.name: MMU_INT_MASK
registers.panthor_write: panthor_mmu_fault_mask(~0) == 0x0000ffff at panthor_mmu.c:3287; per-AS BIT(as) added at :599
registers.note: Matches. Low 16 bits are AS fault enables; bits 16-31 are REQ_COMPLETE and are not maskable.

registers.name: MMU_INT_RAWSTAT interpretation
registers.panthor_write: read; bits 0..15 fault per AS, bits 16..31 REQ_COMPLETE per AS
registers.ours_write: read at many sites; interpreted as MMU_BUS_ERROR(0) in comments :3795-3800, :4330-4340
registers.note: Our runs log 'mmu irq 0x10000' immediately after AS0 UPDATE and call it MMU_BUS_ERROR on AS0. Bit 16 is AS0's REQ_COMPLETE, i.e. the walk finished. Fault latches are bits 0..15 and every run reads as 0 there. This invalidates the 'the walker was refused by the bus' premise used in several comments.

registers.name: AS_TRANSCFG (AS0..AS7)
registers.panthor_write: 0x420001c6 for va_bits=48: PTW_MEMATTR_WB | PTW_RA | ADRMODE_AARCH64_4K | INA_BITS(55-48)
registers.note: Logged readback 'AS0 readback: ... transcfg 0x42000006' (log 244). INA_BITS encodes the input address size to the walker; panthor always programs it. For va_bits=48 the difference is bits 11:6 = 0b011000 vs 0. Untested: whether the MCU's fetch depends on it. Cost to test: one expression, build-flag gated.

registers.name: AS_MEMATTR
registers.panthor_write: derived from the CPU's MAIR by mair_to_memattr()
registers.note: Logged readback matches (log 244). Not a gap; noted because it is the one AS register whose value we cannot independently derive without knowing the CPU MAIR.

registers.name: AS_COMMAND
registers.panthor_write: AS_COMMAND_UPDATE (1) via as_send_cmd_and_wait()
registers.note: Agrees.

registers.name: L2_PWRON
registers.panthor_write: l2_present, through panthor_gpu_power_on(..., L2, 1, 20000)
registers.note: Agrees. READY reads 0x1 in log 187; PWRTRANS 0.

registers.name: GPU_COHERENCY_PROTOCOL
registers.panthor_write: selected_coherency == GPU_COHERENCY_NONE (31) when the device is not DMA-coherent
registers.ours_write: only when !mali_cold or mali_cohnone at :3186-3194; on the cold path it is left alone
registers.note: Log 184: 'protocol trial 692: features 0x1 before 0 after 0 wrote 0'. On the 692 run mali_cohnone=0 and mali_cold=1, so no write happened. panthor would have written 31 here. Untested variable.

registers.name: GPU_L2_CONFIG
registers.panthor_write: read-modify-write with ASN_HASH_ENABLE only when soc_data->asn_hash_enable
registers.ours_write: no write on the cold path (explicit, comment :3210-3218)
registers.note: G610 is architecture 10; the fork's soc_data for mt6895 does not set asn_hash_enable. Log 185-186 confirms bit 24 stays clear. Not a gap.

registers.name: GPU_PWR_KEY
registers.panthor_write: not written on the probe path (only panfrost does this)
registers.panthor_evidence: panthor_gpu.c:63-64 defines it; no write site in the probe path
registers.note: Agrees on the cold path.

registers.name: SHADER_PWRON
registers.panthor_write: written only through panthor_gpu_power_on for the shader domain, which is not on the MCU-start path
registers.note: Per the task brief, shader_ready is not a power indicator; excluded from the failure-surface list as an action.

registers.name: GPU soft reset
registers.panthor_write: only from panthor_device_reset_work (panthor_device.c:144) and panthor_gpu_suspend path; not from panthor_device_init/probe
registers.note: Agrees: panthor does not soft-reset before the first MCU start.

registers.name: CSF shared region base
registers.panthor_write: panthor_vm_create(..., CSF_MCU_SHARED_REGION_START=0x04000000, CSF_MCU_SHARED_REGION_SIZE=0x04000000)
registers.note: Same VA. Size derives from the image, which is smaller than panthor's 64 MiB reservation; not shown to matter.

registers.name: Doorbell CSF_DOORBELL(0)
registers.panthor_write: ring after boot, in panthor_fw_init_global_iface (panthor_fw.c:1085)
registers.note: Agrees in ordering (only after a boot). Never reached because boot fails.

registers.name: Firmware image source
registers.panthor_write: request_firmware("arm/mali/arch10.x/mali_csffw.bin")
registers.ours_write: embedded blob kMaliFirmware[258048], sha256 de22d2fc...f7229a, include at :43, parsed at :1009-1330
registers.note: Image exists and is parsed; 10 sections, shared at 0x4000000, reset vector sp 0x2040000 pc 0x10018ed (log 234). No sha256 check at run time; only a magic + major + size check (:1014-1022).

registers.name: Firmware image load into MCU-visible memory
registers.panthor_write: kernel BO mapped into the FW VM at the section VA, dma_sync_for_device
registers.ours_write: mem_alloc_low() bump allocator from 0x50000000, ml_io_map_unmappable(WCOMB), memcpy + mem_flush at :1070-1092
registers.note: Ours places sections at fixed low physical addresses with a hand-built AArch64 4K table; panthor uses the IOMMU with CPU pages. Log 226-233 shows every leaf valid and coverage complete.

registers.name: Number of firmware sections mapped
registers.panthor_write: skips CSF_FW_BINARY_IFACE_ENTRY_PROT sections entirely (returns 0)
registers.ours_write: maps protected sections with ordinary memory (:1057-1060, :1192)
registers.note: We allocate 0x3000000-0x3040000 (256 KiB) as ordinary rw memory; panthor refuses PROTM sections without the protected allocator. Not shown to matter for a non-protected boot, but it is a real divergence.

registers.name: Interrupt registration (GIC)
registers.panthor_write: devm_request_threaded_irq for job/mmu/gpu/pwr
registers.panthor_evidence: panthor_device.h:587-600 and the four panthor_request_*_irq calls
registers.note: Deliberate (0 interrupt registrations). Cannot by itself prevent the MCU from executing, since the firmware start is a write plus a poll; it only removes the fast path.

absent_from_ours.why: The EB is the owner of MFG power on this SoC (DTS gpueb-support=<1>; vendor gpufreq skips its own power_control path). Panthor's own comment at panthor_device.c:256 says that without it 'panthor reads all-zero ID/features'.

absent_from_ours.item: Ordering: GPUEB handshake before the first GPU register read
absent_from_ours.why: We map and read GPU_ID with no EB handshake at all; our read succeeds (0xa8670004), which proves the block answers but not that its power state is settled.
Removed deliberately at :2895-2902 on the strength of a claim about kbase; the claim is not verified in this audit.

absent_from_ours.item: Runtime sha256 verification of the firmware blob
absent_from_ours.panthor_evidence: panthor relies on the filesystem/firmware loader contract; we embed the blob
absent_from_ours.why: Header carries MALI_FW_SHA256 but nothing checks it. A wrong blob would be silently accepted.

present_in_ours_absent_in_panthor.item: Hand-written AArch64 page tables for the MCU
present_in_ours_absent_in_panthor.why: Panthor delegates this to the IOMMU driver. Our table is correct per the walk dump (log 226-233) but is unverified against a working MCU.

present_in_ours_absent_in_panthor.item: Direct MTCMOS domain writes via SPM 0x1c001000
present_in_ours_absent_in_panthor.why: Panthor uses genpd. On this SoC the vendor's own hand-written path is compiled out when GPUFREQ_PDCv2_ENABLE is set, so our sequence has no upstream equivalent to compare against.
Vendor does this (gpufreq_mt6895.c __gpufreq_pdc_control); panthor does not, because it never powers the block itself.
Vendor does this; no panthor equivalent. Log 170 shows the values landing.

present_in_ours_absent_in_panthor.item: PMIF/SPMI write to enable VSTACK (MT6368 BUCK2)
present_in_ours_absent_in_panthor.why: A regulator write panthor would do through the regulator framework. Log 155-157 shows status 0x6a -> 0x6e (enabled).
